why: After building the array beautiful, every uncovered index asks 'how many values in beautiful are strictly smaller than arr[i]?'. Sort beautiful once and answer each question with bisect_left, which is the core binary-search counting trick.
hints: Two separate jobs: build beautiful and mark which indices of arr were used; then, for every unused index, count smaller values in beautiful.
Counting 'how many are strictly smaller than x' in a sorted list is bisect_left(sorted_list, x). Sort beautiful once.
Skip a pair that repeats an earlier identical pair (this is what makes the published example 9). Build in O(total length), sort in O(B log B), then n binary searches.
pitfalls: Strictly smaller: equal values do not count (bisect_left, not bisect_right).
An index that was used in beautiful has beauty 0 even if it is larger than many values.
An exact repeat of an earlier pair is not added again, but a different pair that overlaps (like [0,0] inside [0,1]) is still appended.
statement:
You are given an integer array arr of length n and an array pairs of m pairs [l, r]. Each pair names the subarray arr[l..r] (both ends inclusive).

Build an array beautiful by concatenating the subarrays named by pairs, in the order given. A pair that is identical to an earlier pair is not added a second time. (The source text is vague here; this is the reading that reproduces the published answer.)

Index i contributed to beautiful if it lies inside any of the pairs. The beauty of index i is:

  • 0 if index i contributed;
  • otherwise, the number of values in beautiful that are strictly smaller than arr[i].

Return the sum of the beauties of all indices.

Worked example. arr = [1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 5], pairs = [[0,1],[3,4],[0,0],[3,4]].

  • [0,1] gives [1, 2]; [3,4] gives [2, 4]; [0,0] gives [1]; the second [3,4] repeats an earlier pair and is skipped.
  • beautiful = [1, 2, 2, 4, 1]. Indices 0, 1, 3, 4 contributed; indices 2 and 5 did not.
  • Index 2 (value 3): values smaller than 3 are 1, 2, 2, 1, so beauty 4.
  • Index 5 (value 5): all 5 values are smaller, so beauty 5.
  • Sum = 4 + 5 = 9.
constraints:
• Not stated in the source; reasonable bounds for practice:
  • 1 <= n <= 10^5, 1 <= m <= 10^5
  • 0 <= l <= r < n
  • The total length of all distinct subarrays is at most about 10^6.
  • -10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
